feedback: Anne's confession follows the pre-vote contradiction exactly: she borrowed a tour group that the docent and route kept outside the private room. It supplies the personal admission of poisoning but no new decisive evidence needed to choose her. Her ending about other adults explaining her absence to children gives the motive a consequence rather than allowing the educational cause to excuse the murder. Monet and Chip also clarify their collateral lies coherently, which reinforces why lying alone was insufficient. The resolution feels earned, although Anne's final-round alibi was easier to isolate than the earlier opportunity field. The emotional landing is concise and appropriately bitter.
